title: Northwest Territories Home Rebates 2026: Arctic Energy Alliance
desc: Northwest Territories home rebates for 2026: Arctic Energy Alliance pays up to $8,000 for wall insulation, 50% up to $2,000 for a wood stove, and up to $20,000 for solar. Every amount sourced.
h1: Home Energy Rebates in the Northwest Territories
sub: A plain guide to what the Arctic Energy Alliance pays NWT homeowners in 2026/27. Each amount comes from the AEA's own pages, read on October 21, 2026.
sections: The Arctic Energy Alliance, a not-for-profit in Yellowknife, runs the home rebates. They are after-purchase mail-in rebates for the 2026/27 fiscal year, April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027. The AEA must receive your application within 3 months of the purchase date on your receipt. A household can get up to two rebates on the same type of product each year, with exceptions for thermostats, ECM pumps, LED lighting and plug-in controllers. Rebates are the same in hydro and non-hydro communities except for LED lighting, and you no longer need to buy in the NWT to get the full amount. Rebates are no longer available on heating systems that use fossil fuels. The main office is at 101-5102 51st Street, Yellowknife, 867-920-3333, toll free 1-877-755-5855. Our Northwest Territories rebate calculator adds up only what is open.

The AEA pays for insulating your home, claimed on its Residential Insulation Rebate Application Form:

Part of the homeRebate
Exterior wallsUp to $8,000
CeilingUp to $1,500
Exposed floor$500
BasementUp to $2,500
Basement header$625
CrawlspaceUp to $2,000

We did not read the AEA's guidelines for how the amounts are worked out by area, so ask the AEA before you plan a job around the top figures.

The AEA pays 50% of the purchase cost, up to $2,000, for a wood stove or a wood pellet stove. The cost does not include installation or accessories. Other products: a programmable thermostat pays 50% up to $150 (up to 5 a year for an individual), an ECM pump 50% up to $500, an automated vehicle plug-in controller 50% up to $150, and a drain water heat recovery system with at least 30% efficiency pays $700. Washers pay $200, ventless dryers $500, and an all-in-one washer and ventless dryer $750.
Solar, biomass and ground-source heat pumps

The AEA's Renewable Energy program funds solar, wind, wood pellet heating, biofuel and ground-source heat pumps. Residents can get up to $30,000 for biomass-fueled heating systems such as wood-pellet boilers, and up to $20,000 for other projects such as solar panels. The rebate is the lower of 50% of eligible costs and a savings calculation. For solar electric, the calculation is $4.00 per watt. Funding is first come, first served, needs pre-approval, and the AEA asks you to contact them before you apply. It can no longer fund grid-connected renewable electricity in communities that use hydroelectricity.

We found no Arctic Energy Alliance rebate for air-source heat pumps on its Energy-Efficient Products or Renewable Energy pages. That is a negative result, not proof that none exists. The AEA's news list includes a June 9, 2026 study of how well heat pumps work in Yellowknife, and Ottawa's National Heat Pump Rebate is expected in early 2027, so check both. See our National Heat Pump Rebate guide.
faq: Is there a heat pump rebate in the NWT?
We found no AEA rebate for air-source heat pumps. Ground-source heat pumps can get up to $20,000 under its Renewable Energy program with pre-approval.
How much does the AEA pay for insulation?
Up to $8,000 for exterior walls, $1,500 for ceilings, $500 for exposed floors, $2,500 for basements, $625 for basement headers and $2,000 for crawlspaces.
How do I apply for an AEA rebate?
Buy the product, fill out the application form and mail it in with your receipt. The AEA must receive it within 3 months of the purchase date.
Does the AEA pay for a wood stove?
Yes. 50% of the purchase cost up to $2,000 for a wood stove or wood pellet stove. Installation and accessories such as the chimney are not included.
Can I get a rebate for solar panels in the NWT?
Up to $20,000 under Renewable Energy, with pre-approval. For solar electric, the rebate uses $4.00 per watt. The AEA no longer funds grid-connected projects in hydro communities.
